messages.subject: Re: Future projections with user-specified environmental variables
messages.subject_clean: Future projections with user-specified environmental variables
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bethany,

I'm not sure that the issue is coming from biomod2- I downloaded an older version of the package which made that warning message go away, but the environmental ordination still didn't work and threw the "Warning: Error in ade4::dudi.pca: na entries in table" error again. Putting the environmental variables in the right order worked like a charm, thank you so much!

On Monday, October 31, 2022 at 10:11:40 AM UTC-5 Wallace Ecological Modeling App wrote:
> I'll take a look into the biomod2 issue.
>
> As for the projection problem, it is probably due in an error importing the future data. The future variables need to be uploaded in the exact order as your original variables. So for example, if you used: bio01, bio02, bio03, and then soil, then the future variables will need to be future bio01, future bio02, future bio03, future soil... You can check back to see what you've uploaded in the window log (I think there will also be a pop up message above the upload option). Be careful using drag & drop, sometimes this will put them in the wrong order (e.g., 3, 2, 1 instead of 1,2,3).
> Hope that helps!
>
> Bethany
>
> On Monday, October 31, 2022 at 3:54:41 AM UTC-4 nolan...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Hi Bethany,
> >
> > I appreciate you answering all my questions- your insight is super helpful! Issue 1 is still happening after implementing your suggestions (I have the most recent version of Wallace and updated the packages). I think the issue may be coming from ecospat. Every time I try to call it, I get this error message:
> >
> > "Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘ecospat’ in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]):
> > namespace ‘biomod2’ 4.1-2 is being loaded, but < 4.0 is required"
> >
> > This doesn't make sense to me, as it seems to suggest I need to go back to an earlier version of biomod2 to make the package function properly? Not sure!
> >
> > Issue 2 has been resolved (no tile issues when I ran Wallace with Microsoft Edge (P.S.- Wallace seems to perform much better in this browser for me!)), but now I'm having yet another issue. Projecting the model to a new spatial extent works beautifully, but when I try to project my model forward in time using my own variables (a combination of bioclim and some soil characteristics), I get the entire polygon lighting up as suitable habitat, with the exception of where bodies of water are present. I re-ran the analyses using only the bioclim variables thinking the soil might have been causing the issue, but this gave me the same results, sans the bodies of water. Additionally, MESS maps showed the entire polygon uniformly lit up at a similarity of -600. This is the case with all three of the species I have testing- all three of them ground-nesting bees largely restricted to the Northeastern United States. I am interpreting this as an erroneous result because it doesn't make sense to me that the entirety of North America in a future extreme climate change scenario would become suitable habitat. Wondering if this is likelier to be an issue with Wallace or my input rasters- what do you think? Thanks again for your time and consideration, I really appreciate it- nobody in my lab or even my department works with species distribution models, so this forum and your expertise is super helpful!
> >
> > Best,
> > Nolan Amon
> >
> > On Sunday, October 30, 2022 at 9:53:04 PM UTC-5 Bethany Johnson wrote:
> > > Hi Nolan,
> > > I've seen both issues you brought up before, hopefully I can help you fix them.
> > > 1. env ordination crash: There has been a lot of recent changes and edits to the Env Space component. Please make sure your version of Wallace is up-to-date (this may require uninstalling and re-installing). The most recent version is v1.9.4-5.
> > > Also try updating the `ecospat`, `ade4`, & `adehabitatHR` packages. Let me know if the problem persists after this.
> > >
> > > 2. grey map tiles: I have this problem with Google Chrome- Is this the web browser you are using? For me, it happens after I download result data, so you can fix it by closing out the download panel bar at the bottom. You can also try resizing the browser window, sometimes this helps the map reset. Whatever you do, don't refresh the page- you'll lose your work!
> > >
> > > Bethany
> > >
> > > On Saturday, October 29, 2022 at 1:26:27 PM UTC-4 nolan...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > Hi Bethany,
> > > >
> > > > I apologize if I should be creating separate threads for all of these issues. I have proceeded with some of my analyses using Wallace v2 and am noticing an issue when it comes to visualizing my models/trying to project these models to future extents. The map becomes a patchwork of gray tiles and map bits, rather than a continuous map. This happens no matter how far I zoom in or out, and makes it very difficult too visualize my map using the Wallace app and to draw polygons for extrapolating my model to new spaces/times. I have had this issue on both my personal and work computers as well. I'm attaching a screenshot so you can get a better idea of what I'm seeing. Any advice you might have would be greatly appreciated- thank you!
> > > >
> > > > Best,
> > > > Nolan Amon
> > > >
> > > > On Wednesday, October 26, 2022 at 1:42:57 AM UTC-5 nolan...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > Hi Bethany,
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks much for your reply. I was totally unaware of Wallace v2, but it seems like this should do exactly what I want! Additionally, it seems like you and the team have made a lot of quality of life improvements and added some great functionality, which I really appreciate.
> > > > >
> > > > > As an aside, I'm wondering if you can help me deal with a crash error I've gotten three times now- while attempting to perform the environmental ordination with two of my focal species and my user-supplied environmental data, I get the errors " Error in x$.self$finalize(): attempt to apply non function" and "Warning: Error in ade4::dudi.pca: na entries in table". The first error only appeared once, while the second error has appeared three times and seems to crash my Wallace session. If you would like my session file from every step prior to this one, please let me know- it appears to be too large to attach in this forum.
> > > > >
> > > > > Best,
> > > > > Nolan Amon
> > > > > On Tuesday, October 25, 2022 at 4:33:53 PM UTC-5 Wallace Ecological Modeling App wrote:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Hi Nolan, thanks for checking in.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Are you running v1? This is the version that is currently on CRAN. It offers the ability to upload your own user variables as environmental data but does not allow user uploads for projecting. It does have capabilities to transfer the model to a new time period using WorldClim future bioclim variables, but this only works if you built the model using WorldClim bioclimatic variables. The future variables need to correspond to the variables you built the model with, so if you uploaded your own variables instead of using WorldClim, the option will disappear.
> > > > > > I think this is what you meant by saying the options were gone, but v2 (which will be on CRAN very soon!) is stable and can be installed through GitHub. (Check out the vignette <https://wallaceecomod.github.io/wallace/articles/tutorial-v2.html> for install instructions & info on transferring to future environments).
> > > > > >
> > > > > >  In v2, the module “Transfer to User Environments” can be used to upload your own future rasters to transfer the model to. Please note: this version has updated the terminology from “project” to the more appropriate “transfer”, since project is commonly used in GIS for changing the map projection; "Project" in v2 is now "Transfer" in v2. To use this module, just make sure your future rasters are named similarly to your initial rasters. (there will be a message regarding proper naming in the window).
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Let me know if this answered your question.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Bethany Johnson
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Tuesday, October 25, 2022 at 1:10:00 AM UTC-4 nolan...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > > Hi folks,
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Forgive me if this is a basic question, as I am just becoming familiar with Wallace and species distribution models. I have moved on from present and future predictions of the distribution of my focal species using Wallace's default settings (19 Bioclim variables) to now providing Wallace some of my own rasters (soil and elevation data) in addition to the Bioclim data to make predictions about the present potential distribution of my focal species.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I'm also interested in projecting the distributions of my focal species into the future using the aforementioned variables. I have the rasters, but am not sure how to generate the model. How might I go about doing this, as the options for "future projection" are gone with user-specified environmental conditions? Thank you for your time and consideration!
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > Nolan Amon
> > > > > > > Ph.D. Student, Department of Entomology
> > > > > > > University of Wisconsin-Madison

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nolan,
I did extensive testing and I couldn't replicate your errors. I am going to need some more information from you to troubleshoot. But first, let's clarify you are in fact using Wallace version v1.9.4.5 and not 1.9.2.2. This is the equivalent of tech support asking, "did you try turning it off and then turning it back on again?" Simple solution, but it might fix all the problems you are having.

If you are using v1.9.4.5, I'd like to know exactly what your methodologies are- are you using your own files for occurrences and environmental? and what steps are you taking before you get to the crash at e-space. and then what models are you using and what environmental data are not working for the future transfer...
If you prefer, you can send me the data you are using to test out myself.
If the files are large and/or you want a little more privacy, you can send this info to the Wallace gmail account (wallac...@gmail.com).

We should be able to get this figured out soon!

Bethany

messages.subject: Error projecting into new time
messages.body_plain:
Hi there!

I'm a teaching assistant for a course where students are encouraged to use Wallace as part of a climate change vulnerability assessment for a species of their choosing. As an introduction to Wallace, students were instructed to follow through the Wallace version 1 vignette using Tremarctos ornatus occurrence data. To preface, ecological niche modeling is kind of out my wheelhouse and I've got a pretty decent working knowledge in R. I worked through the vignette myself on a PC with little issue (after installing a new version of Java), but many students have been encountering the same issue. When they go to project suitability under future climate projections, they encounter an error and are unable to proceed (error attached). Students are following the vignette instructions to a tee: modeling with GBIF T. ornatus occurrence data, using WorldClim climate data, modeling niches with Maxent, and attempting to project to 2070 with RCP 8.5 projections and CCSM4 for the global circulation model.

I've run through the vignette side by side with a student and we were unable to identify the source of the error on her computer. So far, I've checked that people are using the same version of Wallace (1.1.3) and I created an R script where people preemptively install and load most of the packages that Wallace uses (attached).

Any ideas what the issue may be? Thanks for the help in advance!
Penelope

messages.subject: Re: Error projecting into new time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Penelope,
First of all, great to hear about Wallace being used in your teaching! Please give us some feedback via our external curriculum survey <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdR4qVprBBpyEZwF4sAurjKuXrxggEA7jWnINenltnUY3nWnA/viewform>.
I also want to give you a heads up, we are very excited to announce v2 will be up on CRAN very soon!

This error has already been fixed in our new version, so if you wish to try out Wallace v2, check out the new vignette (which includes installation instructions until Wallace is on CRAN) - https://wallaceecomod.github.io/wallace/articles/tutorial-v2.html.

I can see why you might not want the students to have to completely start over, so I think I fixed the problem and you can download the corrected version of Wallace v1.1.3 from my Github for now.
library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/bjohnso005/wallace/tree/v1.1.3")
library(wallace)
run_wallace()

Thanks for letting us know! Please reach out if you are still having trouble, if you have any issues installing, and stay tuned for an update when the new version is officially released!

-Bethany
